newsitem.title: SPAIN: Inespal says effects of strike appear minimal.
newsitem.headline: Inespal says effects of strike appear minimal.

text.p: Spanish aluminium producer Inespal said on Friday that it was still evaluating the effects of 24-hour strike action at its nine plants, but the effects appeared to have been minimal, a spokeswoman said.

"It's very early to say, but where any of the staff were actually working --which was all the plants-- it meant that factories could keep on going. I wouldn't say it had hampered production too much," she said.
Trade unions have called a series of strikes, starting on July 3, to protest at privatisation plans. Local media reported 24-hour strikes had been called for July 10, 17 and 24.

An industry source, who declined to be named, estimated that around 40 percent of the staff at Inespal who were meant to be working on Thursday had gone on strike. But in some plants production was entirely normal, the source estimated.

In local media reports, unions estimated that at least 80 percent of staff had taken part in strikes at Inespal and Corporacion Siderurgica Integral, a steel firm also involved in protest over a planned sale.
Inespal sold 464,527 tonnes of aluminium in 1996, and had net sales of 142.3 billion pesetas. It produced 361,828 tonnes of primary aluminium.
At the Spanish state holding company Sepi, which controls Inespal, no-one was available to comment.
